sections.h2: Ways to sell a Muskego house
sections.html:
Sellers in Muskego pick from an agent, a private sale or a cash buyer who wants the property untouched. Direct sales come up most often for lake homes, for older houses that have gone without repairs and for inherited property.

The city sits in Waukesha County, has 25,602 residents, and about 84.8 percent of homes are owner-occupied. For 2020 to 2024 the median home value was $417,400, median household income was $112,221, and median monthly owner costs with a mortgage were $2,152. Those numbers describe a higher-priced market where repair credits add up fast.

sections.h2: How the lakes shape a sale
sections.html:
Muskego has three lakes within city limits, and the one your house faces changes what buyers ask. Big Muskego Lake spreads over about 2,260 acres in the south-central part of town. It is shallow, mostly under four feet deep, with a muck bottom and cattail marsh along the edges. Little Muskego Lake covers 506 acres, reaches 65 feet at its deepest, averages 14 feet and has houses along most of its shore. Lake Denoon covers 162 acres in the southwest.

  • Waterfront buyers ask about shoreline rules, so find your survey and any records for piers, retaining walls and permits.
  • Describe the lake accurately. A shallow marsh lake and a deep lake with boating, skiing, sailing and fishing attract different people.
  • Before you tell a buyer what can be built or changed near the water, call the Building Inspection Division at (262) 679-4145.

Muskego-Norway School District serves the city. Its elementary schools are Bay Lane, Lakeview and Mill Valley. Lakeview serves Muskego residents even though it sits in the Town of Norway. Middle schools are Muskego Lakes and Lake Denoon, and Muskego High School completes the list. Parochial choices include St. Leonard K-8 Catholic School and St. Paul's Evangelical Lutheran Grade School. The district can tell you which elementary school covers your street. Use that in the listing.

Has your Muskego house hosted guests? Chapter 297 of the city code applies. More than 10 nights of renting in a license year takes a city license, issued by the City Clerk. On top of that come a Wisconsin tourist rooming house license and, unless exempt, a seller's permit from the Department of Revenue.

  • Each license is good for one calendar year, January 1 through December 31.
  • The owner carries liability insurance and must be reachable from 8:00 a.m. to 11:00 p.m. on rental days.
  • Guests sign a register, and the unit cannot go to more than one party within a six-day period.
  • A violation costs $200 to $1,000 per offense, with every day counted separately.

Buyers planning to keep renting can ask the City Clerk about applying in their own name. Settle unpaid city charges first, because the chapter bars issuing or renewing a license while the city is owed money.

You will find the Building and Inspection Services Division at W182 S8200 Racine Ave. Inspectors work Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., while walk-in office hours are Monday, Wednesday and Friday, 8:00 to 9:00 a.m. Call (262) 679-4037 to book an inspection or ask a technical question, and (262) 679-4145 for general permit questions. The division's web page links to code, fee and permit information.

Do you have a finished basement, deck or addition with no closed permit? Call before you list. Inspectors working for buyers can ask for permit records, and a cleared file spares you delays once a contract is signed.

Houses with one to four units come under Wis. Stat. 709.02. You owe the buyer a finished condition report by the tenth day after acceptance. A buyer who is left waiting gets the following two business days to cancel and collect deposits. Section 709.02 also allows you to rest matching entries on written findings from an engineer, surveyor, pest control operator or contractor.

Under Wis. Stat. 77.22 the grantor, meaning you, pays a transfer fee of 30 cents per $100 of value. On a house priced near the city median, that is a four-figure fee, so ask your title company for the exact amount early.

Your deed is recorded in Waukesha County, where standard documents such as deeds and mortgages cost $30. Write the check or money order to the Register of Deeds, because the office will not take cash, credit or debit. A transfer fee, if one is due, goes into the same payment.

Include an email address or a stamped, self-addressed envelope so the recorded document can find its way back to you. Staff cannot give legal advice, which is why a title company or attorney should handle the deed.

First-half payments are due January 31 and second-half payments July 31. A late first installment makes the whole balance delinquent on February 1. Ask the City of Muskego treasurer for the current bill and any special charges before closing, and let the closing agent divide the year's tax.

Assessments follow market value on January 1. Owners who disagree can use the Open Book and Board of Review process, so ask the city assessor for this year's dates.

A lakefront or older Muskego house tends to carry more paperwork than a newer subdivision home, and buyers read it closely. Before listing, set out the following.

  • Your survey, plus records for any pier, retaining wall or other work at the water's edge.
  • Permit and final-inspection records for finished basements, decks and additions.
  • Rental license, register and insurance papers if guests ever stayed, along with proof that city charges are paid.
  • Your mortgage lender's payoff figure and the current tax bill.
  • Written findings from an engineer, surveyor, pest control operator or contractor, which you may rely on for matching condition report entries.

Fewer steps is the appeal of cash. You skip showings, wait on no buyer loan and avoid a repair list negotiated after an inspection. A listing may fetch a higher price from a buyer who finances, at the cost of speed.

  • Request the offer in writing with the closing date.
  • Check what the buyer assumes about repairs and permits.
  • Work out your net after the mortgage payoff, the transfer fee and recording costs.

The condition report, transfer return and recording apply on either route.

faqs.a: Waukesha County, so deeds are recorded with the Waukesha County Register of Deeds. The recording fee for a deed is $30.

faqs.q: Do I need a license to rent my Muskego house short term?
faqs.a: Yes, for more than 10 nights in a license year. Chapter 297 calls for a city license from the City Clerk, a Wisconsin tourist rooming house license and, unless exempt, a Department of Revenue seller's permit.
The city's Building and Inspection Services Division. Call (262) 679-4037 to schedule an inspection or (262) 679-4145 for general permit questions.
Big Muskego Lake, Little Muskego Lake and Lake Denoon lie within city limits. They cover about 2,260, 506 and 162 acres.

faqs.q: Can the Waukesha County Register of Deeds take a credit card?
faqs.a: No. The office takes a check or money order made payable to the Register of Deeds for recording fees.
